types.title: Succession-led acquisitions
types.definition: An owner hands the business to a successor who can carry its people, knowledge and customer relationships forward.
types.suitable: Founders and families weighing who should lead next.
types.objectives: Protect continuity, agree the founder’s future role and plan the handover.
types.role: We discuss what the family wants to preserve, identify potential successors and plan introductions around the owner’s preferences.

types.title: Full and majority business exits
types.definition: A sale of the entire business or a controlling stake, with scope for the owner to retain an agreed interest.
types.suitable: Owners considering retirement, a change of role or a partial exit.
types.objectives: Choose how much to sell, what involvement to retain and which buyer fits.
types.role: We compare ownership routes, agree an approach to buyers and coordinate diligence with the owner’s advisers.

types.title: Family-to-family acquisitions
types.definition: One business family acquires an enterprise from another, often with a shared interest in long-term ownership.
types.suitable: Business families seeking a successor or an adjacent business to own.
types.objectives: Find alignment on culture, stewardship and the outgoing family’s involvement.
types.role: We discuss both families’ priorities and bring them together when expectations on control and continuity align.

types.title: Business continuity planning
types.definition: Preparation for a transfer of ownership while the business keeps serving customers and supporting its team.
types.suitable: Owners whose relationships or operating decisions still depend heavily on them.
types.objectives: Identify key dependencies and agree which responsibilities transfer first.
types.role: We work through the handover with the owners and incoming team, alongside their professional advisers.

types.title: Management-led ownership transitions
types.definition: An existing management team explores taking ownership of the business it already runs.
types.suitable: Experienced managers and owners who want continuity in day-to-day leadership.
types.objectives: Keep operating knowledge in place and clarify future ownership and governance.
types.role: We help the parties define their objectives, explore suitable funding relationships and coordinate the transaction process.

types.title: Entrepreneurship through acquisition
types.definition: An entrepreneur buys and runs an established company, building on its existing team, customers and operations.
types.suitable: Operators, industry specialists and searchers who want to become business owners.
types.objectives: Find a business that fits the operator’s skills and the founder’s succession priorities.
types.role: We help define a search, identify relevant businesses and introduce aligned owners or capital partners where appropriate.

types.title: Business-to-business acquisitions
types.definition: An established company buys another operating business to add a product, capability or customer base.
types.suitable: Promoter-led groups and companies pursuing an acquisition within or alongside their existing operations.
types.objectives: Bring complementary activities under shared ownership and assess how the businesses could work together.
types.role: We translate the buyer’s requirements into a target profile, qualify potential sellers and coordinate introductions.

types.title: Strategic buyouts
types.definition: A corporate buyer takes control of a business that advances a specific growth priority.
types.suitable: Corporate development teams and strategic buyers with a defined capability gap.
types.objectives: Add capacity, enter a product line or secure a critical part of the supply chain.
types.role: We map potential targets to the buyer’s priorities and help both sides evaluate the fit before diligence.

types.title: Roll-ups and consolidation
types.definition: A buyer acquires several complementary businesses around a shared operating platform.
types.suitable: Acquisition teams building a group in a fragmented industry.
types.objectives: Build scale across locations or specialties while assessing how each acquisition can be integrated.
types.role: We define the acquisition criteria, identify potential anchor and add-on businesses, and coordinate discussions with owners.

types.title: Sector consolidation
types.definition: A business combines with peers in the same industry to deepen its market coverage.
types.suitable: Established sector participants seeking greater density or a broader customer mix.
types.objectives: Evaluate overlapping capacity, complementary accounts and integration priorities.
types.role: We map the sector, screen businesses against the mandate and facilitate discussions with interested owners.

types.title: Geographic expansion
types.definition: A buyer enters a new region through an established local business.
types.suitable: Companies seeking regional distribution, operating capacity or customer access.
types.objectives: Understand the value of local relationships, routes to market and regional management.
types.role: We source within the target geography and qualify local businesses against the buyer’s expansion brief.

types.title: Corporate deal scouting
types.definition: A focused search for potential acquisitions against a company’s own buying criteria.
types.suitable: Corporate development teams with a defined mandate and limited local coverage.
types.objectives: Find relevant off-market businesses and understand owner interest before committing resources.
types.role: We agree a search brief, use our origination network to identify prospects and bring forward qualified introductions.

types.title: Private equity buyouts
types.definition: A private equity investor acquires a controlling interest in an established company.
types.suitable: Buyout investors with a defined mandate and owners open to institutional ownership.
types.objectives: Align sector, size, control requirements and plans for the business.
types.role: We source against the investment mandate and coordinate introductions and transaction discussions.

types.title: Micro private equity
types.definition: An acquisition investor focuses on smaller established businesses, often with hands-on ownership.
types.suitable: Specialist buyout firms and acquisition investors with a clear operating thesis.
types.objectives: Find businesses where the investor’s sector knowledge or operating partners could contribute.
types.role: We screen for ownership fit, understand founder priorities and identify relevant operating relationships.

types.title: Family office-led acquisitions
types.definition: A family office acquires a direct ownership stake in an operating business.
types.suitable: Family offices and investment holding companies seeking direct business ownership.
types.objectives: Match sector knowledge, preferred control and intended holding horizon.
types.role: We work from the family’s mandate and introduce owners whose objectives fit its approach.

types.title: Investor-backed ownership transitions
types.definition: An investor supports a change of ownership with an incoming operator or an existing management team.
types.suitable: Investors, operators and founders exploring a shared transition.
types.objectives: Align financial participation, management responsibility and decision-making before an acquisition.
types.role: We identify relevant counterparties and help the parties clarify roles before detailed evaluation.

types.title: Search fund-backed acquisitions
types.definition: A search entrepreneur pursues an established business with the support of acquisition investors.
types.suitable: Search fund teams and investors who back entrepreneurs to own and operate companies.
types.objectives: Find an owner willing to transition and a business suited to the incoming leader.
types.role: We help refine search criteria, surface relevant businesses and coordinate discussions among owners, searchers and investors.

types.title: Foreign buyouts
types.definition: An overseas buyer acquires an Indian business, subject to applicable legal, tax and regulatory requirements.
types.suitable: International strategic buyers, investment firms and business families evaluating Indian ownership opportunities.
types.objectives: Assess local fit and align ownership, diligence and transition expectations.
types.role: We originate Indian businesses against the buyer’s brief and coordinate discussions alongside qualified advisers.

types.title: International strategic acquisitions
types.definition: A corporate acquirer seeks an Indian business that complements its global operations.
types.suitable: International manufacturers and service businesses with a specific capability requirement.
types.objectives: Evaluate manufacturing depth, talent, suppliers or complementary product lines in India.
types.role: We assess the industrial fit, establish owner interest and support coordination across the two teams.

types.title: India market entry through acquisition
types.definition: An international buyer establishes a local presence by acquiring an existing Indian operation.
types.suitable: Businesses comparing acquisition with building a local operation from the ground up.
types.objectives: Assess customers, operating capacity and leadership already in place.
types.role: We define the India entry brief and identify businesses whose footprint fits the buyer’s plans.

types.title: Cross-border sourcing relationships
types.definition: An overseas acquisition team works with a local origination partner to identify potential businesses in India.
types.suitable: International acquisition teams seeking local access and context.
types.objectives: Build a relevant target list and establish whether owners are open to a conversation.
types.role: We connect the search brief with our pan-India origination network and qualify opportunities before introductions.

types.title: India, UAE and Singapore partnerships
types.definition: A focused partner search across our three-market network supports an India-related acquisition mandate.
types.suitable: Buyers, advisers and investors with a specific cross-border requirement.
types.objectives: Identify counterparties with relevant sector expertise, capital or operating capabilities.
types.role: We clarify the mandate and facilitate relevant introductions. Each party evaluates suitability with its own advisers.

audiences.title: You've spent years building it. Let's find the right next chapter.
audiences.intro: A change of ownership begins with a question about the future. Whether you founded the company or are thinking about succession with your family, your priorities shape the conversation.
services: Explore a full exit, a majority sale or a strategic partnership.
Decide what matters for your employees, customers and family after a sale.
Discuss appropriate successors and agree how and when introductions should happen.
Coordinate diligence, negotiations and a considered handover with your advisers.

faqs.q: What if our family is still deciding?
faqs.a: Start with the questions you are considering. We can explore what a successor, strategic buyer or continuing family role might look like before you settle on a route.

faqs.q: What should I share at the beginning?
faqs.a: Your sector, location, broad revenue range and what you would like to explore are enough. You can choose to discuss revenue privately and keep detailed financials for a later conversation.

faqs.q: When would a buyer learn our identity?
faqs.a: We first discuss your disclosure preferences and the purpose of an introduction. Sensitive information belongs in a later, agreed exchange with appropriate confidentiality arrangements.

audiences.title: Your next stage of growth may already exist.
audiences.intro: A company you acquire could bring a manufacturing capability, a distribution network or the team to enter a new region. We work with promoters, corporate development teams and international strategics to define what a target must add.
services: Translate your growth priority into a focused acquisition brief.
Originate off-market targets by sector, capability, geography and size.
Explore vertical integration, complementary product lines and sector consolidation.
Qualify owner interest and coordinate introductions and transaction workstreams.

faqs.q: What makes an acquisition brief useful?
faqs.a: Specify the capability or market you want to add, target geography, indicative budget and preferred level of control. Identify the one or two criteria a target must meet.

faqs.q: Can we search for a series of acquisitions?
faqs.a: Yes. We can help distinguish the first platform business from later additions, then qualify targets against a common roll-up or consolidation strategy.

faqs.q: Can an overseas corporate submit a mandate?
faqs.a: Yes. Share the India entry or expansion objective and the kind of local business you are seeking. Cross-border structures require assessment by qualified legal, tax and regulatory advisers.

audiences.title: Capital meets businesses worth building upon.
audiences.intro: A family office investing its own capital approaches ownership differently from a buyout fund or an operator-backed holding company. We start with your mandate, intended role and the businesses you know best.
services: Source established businesses against your ownership and sector preferences.
Explore direct acquisitions, investor-backed operators and search fund relationships.
Identify potential partners for India-focused acquisition strategies.
Coordinate introductions for your independent evaluation and diligence.

faqs.a: Family offices, private equity and micro private equity firms, holding companies, search fund investors, experienced individual investors and international investment teams can share a mandate.

faqs.q: Am I subscribing to an investment?
faqs.a: This enquiry starts an advisory conversation about your acquisition interests. Legacy Search facilitates introductions and transaction processes. Each investor independently assesses any opportunity.

faqs.q: Can we explore an operator-backed acquisition?
faqs.a: Tell us the sectors you understand, your preferred role and the operator experience you seek. We can assess relevant business and operating relationships against those criteria.

audiences.title: You don't always have to build from zero.
audiences.intro: Entrepreneurship through acquisition means buying a company and running it. An established business brings customers, a team and years of operating knowledge. Your experience shapes what you can contribute as its next owner.
services: Define a search around your operating experience and sector knowledge.
Explore acquiring and running a business independently or with investor backing.
Consider management-led buyouts and founder succession opportunities.
Meet owners and potential partners where your ambitions and capabilities align.

faqs.q: Do I need a search fund to start?
faqs.a: You can begin as an independent operator, entrepreneur, senior executive or industry specialist. Tell us the business you would be equipped to lead and what support you would need.

faqs.q: What should I include about my background?
faqs.a: Share the sectors, teams, plants, products or business units you have run, along with your preferred region and level of ownership involvement.
We review your interests for fit with owners, businesses or potential partners. Conversations depend on mutual interest. Employment, funding and an acquisition are not guaranteed.

audiences.title: Opportunity is everywhere. Help us discover it.
audiences.intro: Industry professionals often hear a founder’s succession question long before a sale process begins. Our pan-India network of 250+ active deal scouts connects that local knowledge with an acquisition team.
services: Introduce an owner considering a transition or a corporate with an acquisition brief.
Identify acquisition-oriented investors and industry-specific consolidation opportunities.
Bring context from your work as an adviser, chartered accountant, consultant or industry professional.
Agree the scope of collaboration and introduction terms before sharing an opportunity.

faqs.q: Can I introduce a single opportunity?
faqs.a: Yes. Use “Introduce an opportunity” and describe the sector, geography and broad ownership objective. Keep identifying details private until you have permission to share them.
We welcome industry professionals, business advisers, entrepreneurs, association members and people developing an interest in M&A origination. We review each profile for fit.
Any commercial arrangement is governed by separately agreed terms. The introductory conversation establishes your role, the scope of work and how an opportunity will be evaluated.

sectors.title: Chemicals and specialty materials
sectors.detail: Product mix, process knowledge, customer qualifications and the facilities needed to meet them.

sectors.title: Healthcare and pharmaceuticals
sectors.detail: Service footprint, manufacturing capability, quality systems and continuity of operations.

sectors.title: Education
sectors.detail: Institutional continuity, leadership, facilities and relationships with students and families.

sectors.title: Automotive and engineering
sectors.detail: Component capability, customer programmes, tooling and the depth of engineering talent.

sectors.title: Consumer businesses
sectors.detail: Brand strength, distribution reach, repeat demand and the economics of individual channels.

sectors.title: Logistics and distribution
sectors.detail: Route density, customer contracts, fleet requirements and the reach of the distribution network.

sectors.title: Technology and business services
sectors.detail: Client relationships, recurring work, specialist talent and the delivery model behind the business.

sectors.title: Hospitality and commercial assets
sectors.detail: Property operations, operator agreements, location economics and the intended ownership structure.
